one_liner: Asana has a broad, OpenAPI-described REST API with OAuth 2.0 and personal access tokens, plus an official vendor-hosted V2 MCP server at mcp.asana.com.
auth_notes: The supplied pages mention tokens obtained through the standard OAuth or PAT flow. Apps are registered in the developer console. MCP tokens only work with the MCP server, so a separate API app is needed for REST calls. Service-account and Enterprise-tier details from the draft are not on the supplied pages and were removed.
access_notes: Anyone can sign in to the developer console and create an app. The supplied pages do not say whether a free Asana plan includes API access, or what rate limits apply. The draft's 150 req/min and paid-only endpoint claims are unverified. The MCP server's Command variant needs a Command license per user.
blocker_notes: No blocker is evident from the supplied pages. Free-plan API access and rate limits could not be verified from them. The sandbox claim was dropped because no supplied page supports it.
